mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, measured by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST growth exceeds +3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in employment, as reflected by PAYEMS, boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment plans, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite a confirmed employment surge (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests supply-side constraints, which typically precede inflationary pressures and can drive positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 200-day rolling mean by more than 10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4%, central bank expectations shift toward accommodative policy, which tends to lift equity valuations and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE crossing the 4% threshold from above.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales ( proxy via GDPC1 ) generate optimism about future earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite two consecutive months of GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the number of job openings (RSAFS) indicates softening labor market conditions, which can reduce growth expectations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) during a period of RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling industrial production (INDPRO) and rising consumer spending (GDPC1) creates a contradictory but reinforcing demand-supply imbalance that predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 200-day rolling mean by more than 5 percentage points in 80% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a sharp rise in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 often exhibits short-term declines as discount rates increase, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: peak of the interest rate hiking cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p-value > 0.05) during a period of rising FEDFUNDS above 5%.
